title: Data Cache for Intermittent Computing Systems with Non-Volatile Main Memory
problem: Energy-harvesting embedded systems with non-volatile main memory (NVM) must checkpoint frequently to cover Write After Read (WAR) data hazards, incurring both high runtime overhead and excessive NVM writes; existing data cache solutions do not integrate WAR detection and require additional hardware or software memory trackers.
motivation: Intermittent computing on energy-harvesting platforms is gaining importance for batteryless IoT sensors and edge devices, but NVM's slow access and high write energy make naive caching approaches inefficient without WAR-aware management.
method: NACHO integrates WAR dependency detection directly into the data cache controller, eliminating the need for a separate memory tracker. When a cached dirty line is read after being written by NVM (a WAR hazard), the cache itself identifies and handles the dependency without a side-channel tracking structure. This co-design reduces checkpoint frequency (because fewer WARs escape detection) and reduces NVM writes (because dirty data is buffered in the volatile cache and written to NVM only at checkpoint time or on eviction), cutting both runtime and write wear.
key_novelty: Embedding WAR dependency detection logic directly into the data cache, removing the external memory tracker required by prior intermittent computing systems.
contributions: NACHO: a data cache architecture with integrated WAR detection tailored for intermittent computing on NVM-based platforms.
54% average reduction in intermittent computing runtime overhead versus state-of-the-art cache-based systems.
82% reduction in NVM writes compared to a cache-less system; 18% average reduction versus prior cache-based systems.
